Part A faculty-wide curriculum and minor rules

Degree track page corroborates the first-year package and examples of faculty-wide choices. The assessment plan corroborates disciplinary learning outcomes and thesis methods, but its thesis annex still cites the older Research Approaches titles and thresholds. Adopted Part B Art. 7.1 explicitly separates cohorts and controls thesis entry for September 2026; Art. 5.1 controls later-year composition over the older web tables.
components: Complete workshops in two different areas chosen from literature, linguistics and language use.
Before starting, complete at least 50 EC from year one, earn at least 100 EC in the degree overall, and pass Research Approaches.
progression: Year one builds Dutch literary interpretation, phonology, syntax, semantics and language history, along with text and cognition and creative writing. The 10 EC faculty-wide choice is a genuine restricted slot.

Year two develops language acquisition and methodology, early modern and modern Dutch literature, stylistics and language use. The workshops span two different areas among literature, linguistics and language use.

Year three includes the 30 EC minor, a second 10 EC restricted faculty-wide choice, argumentation, current Dutch Studies topics and a 10 EC thesis. Part B Article 7.1 requires 50 first-year EC and 100 total EC for the 2026 cohort, plus Research Approaches. The proposed ordinary year order meets these requirements before the final-semester thesis.
